facts.statement: The genus Enaliornis was first described by Harry Seeley in 1876.
Fossils of Enaliornis have been discovered near Cambridge, England.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found near Cambridge, England

facts.statement: Because they lacked specific traits of other hesperornithines, Enaliornis was initially classified as a loon or diver (Gaviiformes).
facts.quote: Due to its lack of certain hesperornithid apomorphies, they were much more "conventional" birds and were initially held to be Gaviiformes (loons/divers)

facts.statement: Enaliornis is believed to have had poorly developed wings.
facts.quote: However, they were believed to not have well-developed wings

facts.statement: Enaliornis likely possessed lobed feet adapted for swimming instead of webbed feet.
facts.quote: Like other hesperornithines, they probably had lobed feet for swimming, rather than webbed feet

facts.statement: It remains undetermined whether Enaliornis had teeth, unlike other members of its order.
facts.quote: Based on the remnants that have been studied, it has not been determined if these birds had teeth like the others from this order

facts.statement: Seeley originally named the genus Pelagornis in 1866, but the name had to be changed because it was already used for a Miocene bird.
facts.quote: Enaliornis was originally named Pelagornis ("sea bird") by Seeley in 1866, but that name was preoccupied by a Miocene bird related to the pelicans

facts.statement: Three species of Enaliornis have been described: the small E. sedgwicki, the medium-sized E. seeleyi, and the large E. barretti.
facts.quote: Three species have been described: the small Enaliornis sedgwicki, the medium-sized Enaliornis seeleyi, and the large Enaliornis barretti

facts.statement: The largest species, Enaliornis barretti, was about the size of a large pigeon.
facts.quote: The size of the largest of the three species was comparable to a large pigeon

facts.statement: Enaliornis lived between 106.3 and 100.5 million years ago during the Albian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Enaliornis belongs to the parent group Hesperornithiformes.

rejected.statement: Enaliornis lived during the late Albian to the early Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous period.
rejected.quote: Enaliornis is a genus of hesperornithine which lived during the late Albian to the early Cenomanian
